primary_question: After fixed quadratic shading removal and variance normalization, is scanner-code radial NPS shape repeat-stable across four independent scans per label, and is any stock-associated separation stronger than exact balanced-label permutations?

pixel_contract.channels: RGB analyzed separately from the infrared alpha channel; alpha is nuisance-only
pixel_contract.code_domain: native scanner code normalized by its crop mean; no unsupported density, linear-light or spectral interpretation

controls: exact balanced stock-label permutations at the scan-group level
RGB and infrared alpha reported separately
normalized spectral shape separated from raw code variance/amplitude
no parameter fitting until repeatability gates are adjudicated

branch_rules.repeatability_fail: close observable NPS source as unstable; do not fit material profiles
branch_rules.repeatability_pass_association_fail: retain one generic scanner-convolved NPS shape candidate only
branch_rules.repeatability_and_association_pass: retain descriptive stock-associated scanner-convolved signatures; any physical or stock-calibrated interpretation remains forbidden

claim_ceiling: same-scanner observable code-domain NPS/ACF feasibility; not emulsion truth, physical grain size/rate, process response, scanner-independent stock identity or product promotion
